chapter: Piano craft and the New York school
title: Relative versus perfect pitch and Helmholtz
summary: He says he is blessed with relative pitch, so out-of-tune instruments do not bother him, and discusses the ear's frequency range.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Well, it's like they had to do when they used the plunger or the mute, isn't it. On trombone, they had to...
Oh yeah. Well, that's a different thing entirely.
Different, but they have to make that adjustment.

So I've seen more guys like that that suffer; they suffer, you know, with an instrument that's not accurately tuned. They do suffer if they've got actual pitch. See, they can tell you what note a glass is, or anything like that. They know, you know. But it bothers them tremendously. So I am blessed with having relative
pitch because it doesn't bother me! You know what I mean? You're playing with your mind, you're making your own... But actually it's a physical thing with some people that have accurate pitch.
It's an asset in one respect, but...
Automatically they try to get the...to sharpen the tone, so you play a half-note higher and try to mix the harmony and make it sound...
Because actually, you almost think the guy is blessed with perfect -- it's wonderful. But it can be...

It can be worse and bothersome, and hurt their ear physically -- just physically. I haven't really gone into it. I do know, like the physicist...Helmholtz, Helmholtz, the German physicist... What did he say...? He said you can't... Of course, the ear... The more octave range you have between two tones, you can't tell the difference. So if you play a C, if you play a C on the bass and a C-sharp way up on the top, it almost sounds the same. See?
But some people can tell the difference. They have that range, you know; that range of hearing. Just like some animals can hear frequencies way out, you know, and that

makes a difference. Like, I didn't hear the frequency, I didn't hear the frequency...I wasn't aware of the frequency in the voice, until I became aware of it, you know, through a bit of study about the vocal mechanism, etcetera.
